topic: Why ice cream gives you brain freeze

candidates.spoken_text: Gulp ice water, and half of people get brain freeze.
candidates.visual_concept: Big glass of ice water with a straw; a burst at the rim.
candidates.tension: it's not a rare thing — it's a coin flip
candidates.first_frame_concept: huge glass of ice water with a red straw
candidates.visual_action: burst pops at the straw at 0.2 s
candidates.why_it_should_work: a concrete number for a feeling everyone knows

candidates.spoken_text: Brain freeze isn't your brain freezing.
candidates.visual_concept: Wincing face, blue pain zigzag over the forehead.
candidates.first_frame_concept: big wincing face with a pain zigzag on the forehead
candidates.visual_action: pain zigzag draws across the forehead at 0.15 s
candidates.payoff_connection: the pain is referred from the palate (f1, f8)
candidates.why_it_should_work: flips the literal reading of the name

candidates.spoken_text: Sip or gulp? One doubles your odds of brain freeze.
candidates.visual_concept: Ice water glass vs ice cream cone with a question mark between.
candidates.tension: viewers pick a side before the answer
candidates.first_frame_concept: glass and cone side by side, question mark between them
candidates.payoff_connection: gulping vs slow eating experiments (f3, f5)
candidates.why_it_should_work: a choice invites a guess, the video settles it

candidates.spoken_text: Cold hits your mouth. So why does your forehead hurt?
candidates.visual_concept: Shocked face, pain zigzag on forehead.
candidates.tension: the pain is in the wrong place
candidates.first_frame_concept: shocked face with forehead pain lines
candidates.payoff_connection: referred pain from the palate (f1, f8)
candidates.why_it_should_work: names the odd geography of the pain

candidates.spoken_text: Eat ice cream fast, and brain freeze doubles.
candidates.visual_concept: Big ice cream cone with speed lines.
candidates.tension: something you do every summer doubles the odds
